architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added BullMQ job provider as a third option alongside existing Inngest and Local providers, maintaining the same abstract BaseJobProvider interface
architecture_decisions.rationale: The existing provider abstraction (BaseJobProvider) was designed for extensibility, making it straightforward to add new implementations without changing client code. BullMQ fits cleanly into this pattern with its own Redis-based implementation while preserving the same API surface.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added Redis service to development Docker Compose and configured environment variables for Redis connection
architecture_decisions.rationale: BullMQ requires Redis as a backing store. Adding Redis to the development environment ensures developers can test the new provider locally. The Redis port (63790) avoids conflicts with default Redis port (6379) that might be in use elsewhere.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created comprehensive documentation for all three background job providers with clear comparison tables and setup guides
architecture_decisions.rationale: Users need clear guidance on choosing between providers based on their deployment scenario (managed vs self-hosted, development vs production). The documentation explains trade-offs and provides concrete examples for each option.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Integrated job routes into existing API routing structure and configured Vite to handle Bull Board static assets
architecture_decisions.rationale: The existing router.ts already handles API routing, so adding the job routes there maintains consistency. The Vite configuration change ensures Bull Board's static CSS files are properly served through Hono without being intercepted by Vite's dev server.
alternatives_considered: Custom static file serving for Bull Board

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added BullMQ, Bull Board, and Redis dependencies while updating existing packages to newer versions
architecture_decisions.rationale: BullMQ requires bullmq and ioredis packages. Bull Board provides monitoring dashboard. Package updates (esbuild, tailwindcss, @types/node) maintain compatibility and security while adding the new functionality.
alternatives_considered: Custom monitoring instead of Bull Board

implementation_summary:
The implementation adds a Redis-backed BullMQ background job provider as a third option alongside the existing Inngest (managed) and Local (PostgreSQL) providers. This addresses limitations of the Local provider for production self-hosted deployments, offering better reliability, concurrency control, and monitoring capabilities.

The approach leverages the existing provider abstraction pattern, making BullMQ a drop-in replacement that implements the same BaseJobProvider interface. Key decisions include using Redis for queue storage (adding it to Docker Compose), implementing a singleton pattern for BullMQ instances, and providing a Bull Board dashboard for job monitoring accessible via /api/jobs/board.

The changes integrate smoothly with the existing architecture: environment variables control provider selection, documentation guides users through the options, and routing changes ensure the dashboard is properly served. The Vite configuration was carefully adjusted to allow Bull Board's static assets through while maintaining existing dev server behavior. This implementation provides a production-ready job processing solution for self-hosted deployments without requiring external SaaS dependencies.
